static_traits.name: Anton
static_traits.family_status: Both parents serve in the military
static_traits.social_status: Living with girlfriend in Salt Lake City; raising two beagles (Chance and Boomer); having some social support but finding it hard to discuss spider fear with his partner
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; never sought treatment or counseling for this fear before
static_traits.language_features: Marked self-deprecation and negative labels ('stupid', 'loser', 'not manly enough'); rather negative and skeptical attitude; concrete expression, clear logic, can describe fear impact; average cooperativeness, willing to try recording thoughts; avoidance tendency and shame present

basic_info.main_problem: I am afraid of spiders; this fear makes me feel like a failure and ridiculous.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because the fear of spiders began to affect my daily life and cause distress.
growth_experiences: Experienced a spider-related incident in childhood, severely frightened; although not remembering all details, has feared spiders intensely ever since, the problem persisting long-term and gradually worsening.

core_beliefs: I am a failure / not manly enough
I am weak, unable to control my fear
I will lose control facing spiders

special_situations.event: Seeing or learning about spiders appearing at home
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I encounter a spider at home, I will lose control, unable to self-regulate
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately fleeing the scene, heightening checks and vigilance, avoiding lingering in rooms that may have spiders, even unable to fall asleep
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I may collapse / lose control, unable to sleep all night

special_situations.event: Knows there are spiders nearby at the workplace (flight-related environment)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If there are spiders in the work environment, I will be unable to focus and may affect work safety and performance
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding work areas, getting distracted, trying detours or delaying tasks to avoid contact with spiders
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will mess up the work; the situation could be serious

special_situations.event: Arguing with girlfriend (she thinks I overreact)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I show fear, others will look down on me, meaning I am not manly enough, useless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces communication on related topics, avoids activities or places where spiders may appear, to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: She finds me ridiculous / useless, the relationship will suffer because of it

special_situations.event: Comparing with others (believing everyone else can handle spiders but he cannot)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot handle spiders like others can, it proves I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-denial, intensifying self-criticism and shame, further avoiding environments where spiders may appear
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Only I cannot do it, I am not as good as others

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be understood and accepted, seen as someone strong who can master fear
core_conflict.fear: Fear of losing control, being mocked or belittled as 'a loser / not manly enough', worried about relationship damage
defense_goal: Lowering the threat of external evaluation through avoidance and self-denial, maintaining surface-level safety and control

object_relations.self_representation: A self that is a shameful, weak failure prone to losing control
object_relations.object_representation: Critical and non-understanding others (mainly the partner), who may look down on him

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to discuss or face the fear of spiders (such as the counselor suggesting exploration and exposure)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes change is hard and the fear is deeply rooted, worried they will lose control or be proven 'very weak'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone is gentle and empathic, acknowledge the reasonableness of their worries; use questions of concretization and small-step advancement, avoid confrontation, invite them to describe a mildest fear situation and assess a bearable attempt.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Being seen as 'overreacting' or hinted at as 'not manly enough' in the intimate relationship
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Internalizing external evaluation as total negation of the self, believing the problem is that he himself is 'useless'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a supportive tone, identifying and labeling self-attacking language; gently questioning to distinguish fact from evaluation, encouraging him to describe concrete events and impacts, gradually rebuilding a more balanced self-statement.

manifestations: Fear limits choices and actions (avoids places and activities)
Unable to focus at work due to fear, needing to detour or delay tasks
Hard to freely express and discuss fear in the intimate relationship
outcomes: Intensified anxiety and loss of control

manifestations: Feeling 'only I cannot cope', when comparing with others feeling inferior and isolated
Hard to discuss fear with girlfriend or the support system, worried about being looked down on

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Measuring himself against the standard 'others can all cope, so should I'
Judging himself with socialized labels like 'loser' and 'not manly enough'

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: In sessions, expresses doubt and reservation, worrying that trying will prove one 'very weak'

positive_force: Willing to seek help and start counseling, with some motivation for change
Can describe trigger situations and impacts clearly, with a self-observation foundation
Having some social support (girlfriend, pets), though currently hard to discuss fear
negative_force: Long-term avoidance and vigilance reinforcing the fear response
Marked self-labeling and shame, lowering self-efficacy
A cognitive tendency toward catastrophizing and predicting the future intensifies anxiety
Comparison with others leads to inferiority and isolation, hindering support-seeking

target_behavior.behavior: Intense fear of and avoidance of spiders (with panic reactions and insomnia)
antecedent: Merely thinking about or learning there are spiders around
Spiders appear at home or being told spiders have appeared
Knowing there might be spiders at the workplace
target_behavior.core_reason: Childhood traumatic experience with spiders reinforcing dangerous interpretations of spiders, developing into catastrophic and out-of-control cognitions
target_behavior.function: Avoids fear and potential danger to gain immediate safety and emotional relief
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired work focus and performance; strained intimate relationships and arguments; daily activities interrupted and narrowed; difficulty falling asleep, increased fatigue
